facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The genus Masiakasaurus was named in 2001 by Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster.
facts.quote: It was named in 2001 by Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus was a small predatory theropod dinosaur that lived in Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus is a genus of small predatory theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus was a small theropod reaching 1.8 to 2.1 meters in length and weighing 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a small theropod, reaching 1.8 - 2.1 m long and weighing 20 kg.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived between 72.1 and 66 million years ago alongside animals like Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus lived from 72.1 to 66 million years ago, along with animals such as Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus belonged to the group Noasauridae, which consisted of small predatory ceratosaurs primarily found in South America.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus was a member of the group Noasauridae, small predatory ceratosaurs found primarily in South America.

facts.statement: Remains of Masiakasaurus were found in the Maevarano Formation in northwestern Madagascar and first described in the journal Nature in 2001.
facts.quote: Remains of Masiakasaurus have been found in the Late Cretaceous Maevarano Formation in northwestern Madagascar and were first described in the journal Nature in 2001.

facts.statement: Additional specimens of Masiakasaurus were described in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, additional specimens of Masiakasaurus were described.

facts.statement: Following the discovery of new material, approximately 65% of the Masiakasaurus skeleton is now known.
facts.quote: With the new material, around 65% of the skeleton is currently known.

facts.statement: The forward-projecting front teeth were long, spoon-shaped, and had hooked edges.
facts.quote: These teeth are long and spoon-shaped with hooked edges.

facts.statement: The skull of Masiakasaurus was long and low, unlike the deep skulls of abelisaurids.
facts.quote: The skull of Masiakasaurus is long and low.

facts.statement: Unlike the S-shaped necks of many theropods, the neck of Masiakasaurus was stiff due to stout ribs and positioned almost horizontally with only a slight curve.
facts.quote: While many theropods have s-shaped necks, the ribs would make the neck rather stiff in Masiakasaurus, and the back of the neck is positioned almost horizontally, giving it only a slighter curve.

facts.statement: Unlike the extremely reduced arms of abelisaurids, Masiakasaurus possessed longer forelimbs.
facts.quote: While abelisaurids have arms that are extremely reduced in size, Masiakasaurus and other noasaurids had longer forelimbs.

facts.statement: It is assumed that Masiakasaurus had four fingers, with the middle two being the longest, similar to other ceratosaurians.
facts.quote: It is assumed that members of this genus had four fingers, with the middle two fingers being the longest as in other ceratosaurians.

facts.statement: In 2002, Carrano et al. placed Masiakasaurus in the family Noasauridae alongside Laevisuchus and Noasaurus.
facts.quote: In the following year, Carrano et al. (2002) placed Masiakasaurus along with Laevisuchus and Noasaurus in the family Noasauridae.

facts.statement: The existence of robust and gracile forms in Masiakasaurus may indicate sexual dimorphism or represent two distinct populations.
facts.quote: These two varieties may be an indication of sexual dimorphism in Masiakasaurus, but they may also represent two distinct populations.

facts.statement: Adult Masiakasaurus knopfleri may have been prey for the large snake Madtsoia madagascariensis, although such large prey would likely have been injurious for the snake.
facts.quote: Adults of Masiakasaurus knopfleri may have been prey for adults of the snake Madtsoia madagascariensis, though such large prey would have been injurious for the snake.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus took 8 to 10 years to reach the size of a large dog.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus took 8 to 10 years to grow the size of a large dog.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus grew at a rate 40% slower than comparably sized non-avian theropods.
facts.quote: This indicates a rate of growth that is 40% slower than that of comparably sized non-avian theropods

facts.statement: Individuals of this genus grew 40% faster than crocodylians.
facts.quote: individuals in this genus grew 40% faster than crocodylians.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived in what is now Madagascar.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Madagascar.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus knopfleri is the only known species in the extinct genus Masiakasaurus.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus knopfleri es la única especie conocida del género extinto Masiakasaurus

facts.statement: Adult Masiakasaurus knopfleri reached an estimated body length of 1.8 to 2 meters.
facts.quote: M. knopfleri alcanzó una longitud estimada del cuerpo adulto de alrededor de 1,8 a 2 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, the front teeth of Masiakasaurus knopfleri projected forward instead of downward.
facts.quote: A diferencia de la mayoría de los terópodos, los dientes frontales de M. knopfleri se proyectaron hacia adelante en lugar de hacia abajo.

facts.statement: The unique dentition of Masiakasaurus suggests a specialized diet that may have included fish and other small prey.
facts.quote: Esta dentición única sugiere que tenían una dieta especializada, que tal vez incluía peces y otras presas pequeñas.

facts.statement: Other skeletal bones indicate that Masiakasaurus were bipedal with forelimbs much shorter than the hind limbs.
facts.quote: Otros huesos del esqueleto indican que Masiakasaurus eran bípedos, con extremidades anteriores mucho más cortas que las posteriores.

facts.statement: The first four lower jaw teeth project forward, with the first tooth angled only 10 degrees above the horizontal.
facts.quote: Los primeros cuatro dientes dentados de la mandíbula inferior se proyectan hacia adelante, con el primer diente en ángulo solo 10 ° por encima de la horizontal.

facts.statement: These front teeth are long, spoon-shaped, and have hooked edges.
facts.quote: Estos dientes son largos y en forma de cuchara con bordes enganchados.

facts.statement: These teeth have carinae, or sharp edges, that are weakly serrated.
facts.quote: Tienen carinas, o bordes afilados, que están débilmente aserrados.

facts.statement: The skull of Masiakasaurus is long and low.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Masiakasaurus es largo y bajo.

facts.statement: Unlike the very deep skulls of abelisaurids, the Masiakasaurus skull is long and low.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los cráneos de abelisáuridos, que son muy profundos, el cráneo de Masiakasaurus es largo y bajo.

facts.statement: Thick neck ribs would have made the neck quite rigid in Masiakasaurus.
facts.quote: las costillas harían que el cuello fuera bastante rígido en Masiakasaurus

facts.statement: The rear part of the neck was placed almost horizontally, giving it only a slight curve.
facts.quote: la parte posterior del cuello se coloca casi horizontalmente, dándole solo una curva más leve.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus and other noasaurids had longer forelimbs.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus y otros noasáuridos tenían extremidades anteriores más largas.

facts.statement: The humerus is thin and the known hand bones are relatively short.
facts.quote: El húmero, hueso de la parte superior del brazo, es delgado y los huesos conocidos de la mano son relativamente cortos.

facts.statement: Members of this genus are thought to have had four fingers, with the two middle fingers being the longest like in other ceratosaurians.
facts.quote: Se supone que los miembros de este género tenían cuatro dedos, siendo los dos dedos del medio los más largos como en otros ceratosaurios.

facts.statement: Remains of Masiakasaurus were first described in the journal Nature in 2001 from Late Cretaceous deposits in northwestern Madagascar.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado restos de Masiakasaurus en la Formación Maevarano del Cretácico Tardío en el noroeste de Madagascar y se describieron por primera vez en la revista Nature en 2001.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2001 by paleontologists Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado en 2001 por Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano y Catherine A. Forster.

facts.statement: The genus name means "vicious lizard" because the Malagasy word masiaka translates to "vicious".
facts.quote: En malgache, masiaka significa "vicioso", así, el nombre del género significa "lagarto vicioso".

facts.statement: The species knopfleri is named after musician Mark Knopfler, whose music inspired the expedition team.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Masiakasaurus knopfleri, lleva el nombre del músico Mark Knopfler, cuya música inspiró al equipo de la expedición.

facts.statement: Its unique dentition suggests a specialized diet that may have included fish and other small prey.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus lived approximately 70 million years ago alongside animals such as Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus was a member of the Noasauridae group, small predatory ceratosaurs found mainly in Gondwana.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus era miembro del grupo Noasauridae, pequeños ceratosaurios depredadores que se encuentran principalmente en Gondwana.

facts.statement: Fragmentary bones comprising about 40% of the skeleton were collected near the village of Berivotra.
facts.quote: Se recolectaron huesos fragmentarios que comprenden alrededor del 40% del esqueleto cerca de la aldea de Berivotra.

facts.statement: In 2002, Carrano and colleagues placed Masiakasaurus in the family Noasauridae alongside Laevisuchus and Noasaurus.
facts.quote: En el año siguiente, 2002, Carrano et al. colocaron a Masiakasaurus junto con Laevisuchus y Noasaurus en la familia Noasauridae.

facts.statement: In 2002, Carrano and colleagues distinguished two forms of Masiakasaurus: a robust form and a gracile form.
facts.quote: Carrano y col. en 2002 distinguieron dos formas de Masiakasaurus , una forma robusta y una forma grácil.

facts.statement: A right scapulocoracoid specimen of Masiakasaurus has holes that may be puncture marks from predation or scavenging.

facts.statement: Majungasaurus, a large abelisaurid from the Maevarano Formation, may have hunted Masiakasaurus.
facts.quote: Majungasaurus, un gran abelisáurido de la Formación Maevarano, puede haber cazado a Masiakasaurus.

facts.statement: Various feeding behaviors have been proposed for Masiakasaurus based on its unusual dentition.
facts.quote: Se han propuesto varios comportamientos de alimentación para Masiakasaurus sobre la base de su dentición inusual.

facts.statement: Because its front teeth were suited for grasping, Masiakasaurus may have consumed small vertebrates, invertebrates, and possibly even fruit.
facts.quote: Debido a que los dientes frontales habrían sido adecuados para agarrar, Masiakasaurus pudo haber consumido pequeños vertebrados, invertebrados y posiblemente incluso frutas.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus took 8 to 10 years to grow to the size of a large dog.
facts.quote: Masiakasaurus tardó 8 a 10 años en crecer el tamaño de un perro grande.

facts.statement: The time range for Masiakasaurus is the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Masiakasaurus is Noasaurinae.

facts.statement: Masiakasaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
